text:
[gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/html/2308.07192v1) combines more negatives with generalized BCE; its headline gain therefore cannot isolate loss effects. Stronger evidence comes from its MovieLens-1M factorial comparison: BCE, gBCE and sampled softmax at matched negative counts {1,4,16,64,256}. gBCE helps most with few negatives; at 256, SASRec NDCG@10 is similar across losses: 0.1674, 0.1703 and 0.1660, respectively. This supports a loss–sampling interaction, not universal superiority of one objective. These experiments do not establish transfer to the four Amazon categories or isolate temperature, duplicate handling and history exclusion.

For attribution, use matched architecture, initialization, training examples, negative draws/counts, optimization budget and checkpoint selection; vary loss first, then sampling separately. Specify BCE positive/negative weighting, softmax temperature and sampling-probability corrections. Distinguish corrected sampled softmax from uncorrected cross-entropy over sampled candidates. Duplicate negatives repeat gradient contributions; deduplication changes effective count. Full-training-history exclusion changes the negative distribution and possible false negatives; it requires a separate ablation using only permitted training interactions. gSASRec’s calibration theorem assumes uniform sampling with replacement, so altered sampling requires reconsidering its assumptions.

[Sampled-metric research](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) shows that sampled rankings can reverse full-catalog model comparisons even in expectation. Thus HR@10 against 99 negatives measures the pinned candidate task, not full-catalog retrieval. Here, one changed hit moves category HR by 0.5 percentage points and four-category macro HR by 0.125 points. Fixed users/candidates enable paired comparisons but cannot establish robustness to other samples. Repeated checkpoint/hyperparameter selection invites [validation overfitting and optimistic selection bias](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html); report search extent, paired uncertainty and category results, while reserving held-out evaluation for final confirmation.
